note.note:
Medical History

- Current health issues and chronic disease risk factors (e.g., hypertension, diabetes):  3-day history of acute diarrhea (initially watery, now very loose) with prominent vomiting and subjective fever; periumbilical crampy abdominal pain triggered by urge to defecate; no blood in stool or urine; no rash. Sick contact: brother with similar illness; possible local school outbreak. No chronic medical conditions reported.  
- Family history of chronic conditions (e.g., CVD, diabetes):  Not recorded.  
- Current medications including OTC and traditional medicines:  Vitamin D daily (dose/route not documented); ibuprofen as needed for menstrual cramps (dose/route/frequency not documented); oral rehydration solution (ORS) approximately three times daily for 2 days (dose/route not documented).  
- Immunisation status reviewed (flu, COVID-19, pneumococcal, shingles, tetanus):  Not recorded.  
- Sexual/reproductive health status and risks:  Last menstrual period ~2 weeks ago; not sexually active; not using contraception.  
- Lifestyle: physical activity, diet, tobacco, alcohol, substance use:  Physical activity not recorded; diet: “eats well normally”; tobacco: non-smoker; alcohol: occasional pint; illicit substances: denies.  
- Hearing and vision concerns:  Not recorded.  
- Mood, mental health, and risk assessment (depression, anxiety, self-harm):  Not recorded.  
- Social context: family support, caregiving, housing, financial stressors:  Lives with brother and mother; works as a graphic designer; working from home due to illness; brother currently symptomatic with similar illness.  

Examination

- Vital signs: BP, pulse rate and rhythm:  Not recorded (telehealth; no home measurements).  
- Anthropometry: height, weight, BMI, waist circumference if indicated:  Not recorded.  
- Oral health: gums, teeth, dentures if relevant:  Not recorded.  
- Ear exam including otoscopy:  Not recorded.  
- Eye exam: visual acuity, pupil response, fundus if indicated:  Not recorded.  
- Urinalysis: dipstick for protein, glucose, ketones, blood:  Not recorded.  

Investigations (as indicated)

- Blood tests: fasting glucose and lipids preferred; HbA1c if diabetes present/suspected:  Not recorded.  
- Renal function and liver function tests if clinically indicated:  Not recorded.  
- ECG if cardiac risk factors present or baseline:  Not recorded.  
- Cervical screening if eligible and due:  Not recorded.  
- Mammography if eligible and not up to date:  Not recorded.  
- Faecal occult blood test if due:  Not recorded.  
- Bone density (DEXA) if osteoporosis risk present:  Not recorded.  

Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Summary: Acute gastrointestinal illness characterized by watery-to-loose diarrhea, frequent vomiting (including liquids), subjective fever, and periumbilical cramping. Sick contact at home and reported school outbreak. No red flags of GI bleeding. Passing urine about an hour prior to consult; unable to check temperature; no recent travel.  
- Working diagnosis: Acute infectious gastroenteritis, likely viral (norovirus), with risk of dehydration.  
- Supporting DDx (consistent with transcript):  
  - Viral gastroenteritis (High likelihood): Classic abrupt onset with vomiting, watery diarrhea, fever, and household exposure/outbreak; no travel; no blood.  
  - Bacterial gastroenteritis (Medium likelihood): Persistent symptoms >48–72 hours with fever and abdominal pain; stool testing appropriate to exclude.  
  - Dehydration secondary to GI losses (Medium likelihood): Vomiting of nearly all intake and multiple diarrheal episodes; still producing urine suggests not yet severe.  
- Considerations: Acute appendicitis (Low likelihood) given periumbilical pain but atypical overall picture with prominent diarrhea and lack of focal RLQ findings.  
- Plan:  
  - Arrange urgent in-clinic appointment for hydration assessment and to submit stool sample for microbiology.  
  - Continue ORS with very small, frequent sips; simple foods only (e.g., toast/biscuits); avoid fruit, vegetables, and milk as advised.  
  - Safety-net: If feeling more unwell or unable to maintain hydration, attend the emergency department (ED).  
  - Medications: None prescribed during this telehealth visit.  
  - Monitoring: Patient to call back if worsening prior to appointment.  

Health Promotion & Planning

- Education on chronic disease prevention and lifestyle modification:  Advice provided on hydration strategies with ORS and temporary dietary modification during acute illness.  
- Patient health goals and priorities:  Not recorded.  
- Eligibility for GP Management Plan (GPMP) or Team Care Arrangements (TCA):  Not recorded.  
- Referrals (allied health, Quitline, AOD services, Aboriginal health worker, or social supports):  Urgent clinic appointment arranged for assessment and stool sample; ED if deterioration.  
- Follow-up and recall appointments scheduled:  Urgent appointment to be booked through support line; patient advised to return/seek ED care if worsening.  

Consider

- Mental health support or counselling referral:  Not recorded.  
- Specialist referral for complex chronic disease management:  Not recorded.  
- Dental referral if oral health issues identified:  Not recorded.  
- Optometry referral for visual concerns or regular screening:  Not recorded.  
- Audiometry referral if hearing issues suspected:  Not recorded.  
- Social work or housing support referral if social determinants affect health:  Not recorded.  

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)
- Viral gastroenteritis (High): Acute vomiting and watery diarrhea with subjective fever and clear sick contact/outbreak; no blood or travel.  
- Bacterial gastroenteritis (Medium): Persistent symptoms with fever/abdominal pain; stool testing warranted to exclude bacterial pathogens.  
- Dehydration due to GI losses (Medium): Ongoing vomiting and diarrhea with poor oral intake; still urinating suggests not yet severe but at risk.

Quality checks
- Missing but clinically expected elements: Vitals (including measured temperature), BMI/anthropometrics, immunization review (influenza, COVID-19, pneumococcal, shingles, tetanus), chronic disease screening (lipids, glucose/HbA1c), urinalysis, and preventive cancer screenings (cervical, mammography, FOBT) not recorded.  
- Internal conflicts or contradictions: Patient’s DOB (1984) indicates age ~40; template requested is for adults 55+ (context mismatch noted).  
- Transcript quality notes: Several brief pauses/inaudible segments; telehealth format limited physical examination and vitals.
